scope: Independent read-only architecture review of raw trigger diagnostics. No production edits, child agents, firmware flashing, connected ESP32 execution, or physical qualification.
result: Early review complete. Concrete findings and reproductions were sent to parent during implementation. Group1 isolation resolves the initial decoder-front-end design regression. Remaining fixes are in progress; this artifact is not final-source or final-ELF approval.

findings.status: Architecture reworked by parent; final build review pending
findings.location: engine_target.cpp: capture channel polarity configuration and on_capture
findings.finding: Enabling positive and negative capture on the existing decoder channels changes the decoder front end despite queuing only positive callbacks. A negative edge can overwrite a pending positive-edge latch. SDK also reads timestamp and polarity in separate MMIO operations, allowing a mixed pair if another edge arrives between reads. Both-edge ISR load persists even when recorder is idle in the initial design.
findings.evidence: mcpwm_capture_default_isr clears status and reads cap_value then cap_edge. S3 cap_chn register is documented as last capture; cap_status stores last edge, without a FIFO.
findings.resolution_review: Dedicated group1 capture timer plus independent CaptureClock and two diagnostic channels is appropriate. Preserve group0 rising-only configuration and baseline decoder callback. Diagnostic mapping errors must not trip the executor. Do not allocate/enable group1 in dummy-load or legacy-pulse physical builds.

findings.finding: Per-row frame-ID checks miss a rearm immediately after the last row read, before row serialization completes. Old rows are returned with snapshot_superseded=false despite frame change during snapshot.
findings.reproduction: architecture-probe.cpp re-arms inside the reader immediately after successfully reading row16/16. Result: returned_id=1,current_id=2,returned_rows=16,snapshot_superseded=false. Rearming after row4 is correctly detected and all rows discarded.
findings.resolution_review: Final frame-ID validation after the last record copy/serialization establishes a clear snapshot boundary. Apply it to zero-row metadata reads as appropriate. UI must gather only a frozen same-ID frame.

findings.status: Parent implementing64-row paging, metadata-only default and checked JSON allocation
findings.finding: Unchecked cJSON allocation failure can return a partially built frame as a successful JSON response. Initial full512-row tree also has substantial transient heap cost.
findings.reproduction: With cJSON hooks denying allocations after400 attempts, declared_count=512 but only21 rows return, one incomplete, and snapshot_superseded is absent. Native full512 frame is76532 encoded bytes and peaks at560474 requested heap bytes including encoding.
findings.target_layout: Pinned Xtensa compilation confirms Record=32 bytes,Capture=16432 bytes,cJSON=40 bytes; native cJSON=64 bytes. Native peak is not a target measurement. Target ABI reduces tree cost but full-frame peak remains material, especially non-PSRAM web builds.
findings.resolution_review: Metadata-only default and bounded64-row pages avoid full-frame construction. Check every required JSON allocation/attachment and return an explicit error instead of partial records; bound encoding memory too.

findings.status: Parent implementing invalid-map drop/count and considering explicit group1 pending-status clear
findings.location: trigger_log.hpp: Capture::append; engine_target.cpp: diagnostic start/disable lifecycle
findings.finding: SDK channel disable disables capture and interrupt service but does not clear pending capture status. Re-enable may deliver a previous-session latch. Current prearm guard checks only valid mapped timestamps; an invalid old mapping is accepted as a new invalid row. After a full32-bit wrap an arbitrarily old latch can alias a recent valid time.
findings.reproduction: architecture-probe.cpp passes an invalid-time candidate after arming; returned_rows=1 and prearm_ignored=0. Source inspection confirms mcpwm_capture_channel_disable does not clear status.
findings.resolution_review: Drop/count invalid mappings. Clearing only group1 capture status bits immediately before new frame start is appropriate while both diagnostic channels and both interrupt handles are confirmed disabled, serialized by trigger_mutex. Keep valid-time prearm filtering because an already in-flight SDK callback can survive a clear. Do not hold target portMUX across driver enable/disable.

findings.status: Parent acknowledged extraction to ecu/json.hpp; rerun compile when landed
findings.finding: New public header includes config_json.hpp from firmware/main, which is not a configured component include directory. Pinned target compilation of engine_target.cpp fails to resolve it.
findings.evidence: architecture-object-compile.log records fatal error: config_json.hpp: No such file or directory. Native probe deliberately adds -I firmware/main, so it does not disprove target failure.
findings.resolution_review: Extract shared helpers to a proper include location or separate request parsing from frame serialization.

findings.status: Parent reported fix; final compilation pending
findings.finding: Pinned IDF mcpwm_soft_sync_config_t is empty; assigning software.group_id=1 is invalid.
findings.resolution_review: Remove assignment. mcpwm_capture_timer_set_phase_on_sync binds a soft-sync source to the capture timer group.

findings.status: Reported to parent for ISR audit update
findings.location: scripts/audit_target_isr.py: root discovery and root-count assertion
findings.finding: Existing audit discovers on_capture/on_alarm plus two driver handlers and expects4 roots. It omits new on_trigger_capture, allowing the new callback closure to go unaudited.
findings.resolution_review: Add diagnostic callback as explicit fifth root in selected builds; keep4 roots and verify diagnostic callback absence in physical builds. Audit its functions, literal loads, record/clock/context DRAM placement, and allocation/math closure in the final linked image.

positive_design_findings: Capture frame is finite and never overwrites frozen rows. Header reset does not clear the16KiB data array under the target lock.
Record copies and header access use bounded short locks. JSON allocation/formatting happens outside the target portMUX.
Stop is bound to an explicit frame ID and is idempotent for the same frozen current frame; stale stop cannot stop a newer frame.
Configuration epoch is stored per record; saves need not rearm or discard a diagnostic frame. Epoch should be described as callback-time configuration epoch.

Proposed diagnostic task mutex serializes enable/disable/start/stop. Current worker takes it nonblocking, then re-reads the frame state; this avoids disabling a newer frame based on an older observation.
Pinned esp_intr_enable/disable support cross-core control of these muxed peripheral interrupts; core1 allocation with HTTP-task control is permitted.
required_lifecycle_contract: Keep diagnostic capture timer running between sessions, with channels disabled; if stopped/reset, re-synchronize the independent CaptureClock before accepting records.
Allocate/register diagnostic resources once on the intended core. Group1 priority1 is independent of group0/timer priority3 and reduces timing interference.
Driver controls and blocking task mutex waits must remain outside target portMUX and outside ISR.

Before rearm: acquire trigger_mutex, confirm prior frame not armed, disable both old diagnostic channels, clear their pending status while disabled, then establish new frame start and enable channels.
On stop/full/timeout: freeze frame under target lock; worker or HTTP task disables channels under task mutex and rechecks current frame state after acquiring it.
On diagnostic allocation/sync/control failure: expose availability/error and preserve group0 operation; never enable physical outputs or clear an executor fault.
remaining_hardware_measurement_limits: No ESP32 was connected or flashed. Target ISR latency, lock hold time, cross-core timing and cleanup latency are unmeasured.

Dedicated group1 isolates decoder latches but does not make the diagnostic latch a FIFO or atomically pair timestamp/polarity. Capture overwrite, coalescing, timestamp/polarity mismatch and missed edges remain unmeasured.
A finite buffer bounds record storage, not interrupt load or time to disable under arbitrary noisy/high-frequency input. Physical builds must omit diagnostic interrupt allocation.
Software-sync bracket uncertainty, shared APB rate behavior and32-bit counter wrap need hardware validation with independent stimulus/timestamps.
Records show SDK-reported conditioned digital input events, not analog waveform levels or actual injector/coil output edges. Cam phase is not decoded.
Raw web diagnostics are progress toward logger coverage, not TunerStudio high-speed logger protocol compatibility or complete Speeduino feature parity.
next_validation: Re-run portable recorder/JSON tests including final-read rearm, invalid stale latches, every allocation failure point and page assembly. Build selected and physical modes; inspect final ELF callback roots and diagnostic resource exclusion. These remain pending implementation completion.
